chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-'Asimi narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Mithami, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Yusuf, from Mathanna ibn al-Walid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام.

He was asked about a man who appointed another man as guardian over his children and wealth belonging to them, and at the time of the bequest gave him permission to conduct business with the wealth, with the profit being between him and them. So he said: There is no harm in it, because their father had given him permission for that while he was alive.

key_terms.أَوْصَى: appointed through a bequest or will
key_terms.الرِّبْحُ: the profit الناتج from investment or trade
key_terms.الْوَصِيَّةِ: the bequest or will in which authority is assigned
key_terms.بِوُلْدِهِ: concerning his children placed under another's care
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no legal objection to it
key_terms.مَالٍ: property or wealth belonging to the children
key_terms.يَعْمَلَ بِالْمَالِ: to transact or invest using the wealth

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a guardian to invest orphaned children's wealth and share in the profit if the father authorized it before his death?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a guardian appointed over children and their property. It states that there is no harm in the guardian investing the children's wealth and sharing profit with them if the father explicitly authorized this during his lifetime.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5538 - Muhammad ibn Ya'qub Al-Kulayni, may Allah (swt) be pleased with him, narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad Al-'Asimi from Ali ibn Al-Hasan Al-Mithami from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf from Mathanna ibn Al-Walid from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Abdullah (as), who was asked about a man who appointed another man as the guardian over his children and their wealth. He also permitted him, in his will, to invest the wealth with the profit being shared between him and the children.
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in that because their father had granted him permission to do so while he was alive."
